# **9\. The biggest issue: Keyword cannibalization**

I noticed that you have multiple URLs around similar topics.

For example:

```
/guides/best-free-llm-apis

/ai-tools/free-apis

/ai-tools/llm-apis
```

These pages could compete for similar searches.

I would give each a completely different purpose.

| Page | Primary purpose |
| ----- | ----- |
| Best Free LLM APIs | Editorial comparison and recommendations |
| Free APIs | Filterable directory of free APIs |
| LLM APIs | Broader directory including free and paid providers |

Do not blindly delete or merge them.

First, inspect the queries for each URL separately in Search Console. If they satisfy essentially the same intent and provide overlapping content, consolidate or differentiate them.

# **11\. Technical and content improvements**

These should apply across the website.

Content quality

Every important guide should have:

* An accurate author/byline.  
* Date published and last updated.  
* Sources for factual claims.  
* Original screenshots where appropriate.  
* Examples with transparent assumptions.  
* Unique insights or testing methodology.  
* Direct answers to search intent.

Google explicitly emphasizes original analysis, factual accuracy, visible authorship and genuine usefulness. It also warns against generating large amounts of unoriginal content just to manipulate rankings.

Google for Developers+1

This is why I would abandon the idea of publishing 400 articles rapidly.

Internal linking

Use this architecture:

```
                 MAIN TOOL
                    |
          ---------------------
          |         |         |
       Guide 1   Guide 2   Guide 3
          |         |         |
          ------- Related -------
                    |
              Other relevant
                 resources
```

Use contextual links rather than inserting the same repeated links everywhere.

Technical SEO

Check:

* Canonical URL correctness.  
* Indexability of important pages.  
* XML sitemap coverage.  
* Broken internal links.  
* Duplicate titles and descriptions.  
* Mobile usability.  
* JavaScript-rendered main content.  
* Page loading performance.  
* Proper breadcrumbs.
